ours: vendor/ssh-fuzzer mapper + PSM patches P1-P5 (Paramiko-based, DH group14-sha256, rsa-sha2-256, publickey auth, non-strict KEX)
theirs: vendor/agentic-protocol-state-learning @ 76b49e1 src/smlearn/ssh/mapper.py (curve25519, ed25519, password auth), timeout 0.4 s / quiet 0.1 s as in their v3vm runs

KEXINIT.rationale: Both send SSH_MSG_KEXINIT (20). Ours: fixed cookie per connection (P4), offers group14-sha256; theirs zero cookie, curve25519.

KEX30.rationale: Both send message 30: ours KEXDH_INIT (DH group14), theirs KEX_ECDH_INIT (curve25519). Same message number and protocol role.

NEWKEYS.rationale: Both send SSH_MSG_NEWKEYS (21). Difference: ours re-derives old keys when no KEX completed since the last NEWKEYS (stream corruption, psm/taint.py); theirs keeps the current keys (MAPPER-SPEC).

UA_PK_OK.rationale: Both a correct USERAUTH_REQUEST for user tester, service ssh-connection; ours method publickey with signature, theirs method password. Mapped as 'successful authentication'; method-specific behaviour is not comparable.

CH_OPEN.rationale: CHANNEL_OPEN session in both. Ours allows only one channel (second gives mapper-made CH_MAX without sending); theirs always sends.

inputs_not_mappable.rationale: No counterpart in our learned alphabets A/B (our mapper crashes on the CH_* inputs, vendor/PATCHES.md).

CLOSED (alone).rationale: Theirs reports the close in the step where it happens as CLOSED and NO_CONN afterwards; ours reports NO_CONN in both.

X+CLOSED.rationale: Ours does not show a TCP close that happens in the same step as a message (report.md, 'abstraction hides').

first step.ours: strip the leading KEXINIT token of our first output (NO_RESP if nothing remains)
first step.rationale: Theirs absorbs the server KEXINIT in reset(); ours reports it in the first step.

KEX31+NEWKEYS(+EXT_INFO).rationale: Both mappers report the server reply and NEWKEYS bundled in the KEX30 step; names identical.

EXT_INFO.rationale: Server EXT_INFO (RFC 8308) is sent only if the client KEXINIT advertises ext-info-c; ours (Paramiko) does, theirs does not (observed in results/v2/A/tm_smoke.json). Setup difference, not behaviour.

not_mappable.CH_MAX (ours): mapper-made, nothing sent; any comparison at or after it is skipped
not_mappable.first input other than KEXINIT: ours then sends its own KEXINIT automatically, theirs never does: different concrete messages; compared but every mismatch is classified 'setup: auto-KEXINIT'
not_mappable.steps after our NEWKEYS without a comple: our stream is corrupted (psm/taint.py); a mismatch there is classified 'ours wrong (known, taint)'
